text.p: U.S. diagnostics company Selfcare Inc won its battle on Friday to replace the board of troubled British healthcare company Enviromed Plc.

Selfcare, which owns nearly 29 percent of the voting shares in Enviromed, succeeded in persuading other shareholders to support its call to replace Enviromed's board, including managing director Thomas Murphy.

At an extraordinary general meeting, a Selfcare motion to replace the board was carried overwhelmingly on a show of hands. Sources said the board had conceded defeat and the new board, which includes Selfcare chief executive Ron Zwanziger, was currently meeting. Selfcare had accused Enviromed's board of running down the value of the company through poor management. Enviromed's share price has plunged from around 112 pence in December 1994 to around 25 pence.
Enviromed produces specialist enzymes for diagnostic and research use and is devising ways of detecting heavy metals in entities like water, blood and earth.
Most of Enviromed's shares are held by institutions including Britain's Equitable Life Assurance Society. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
